_comment: The gateway mapping for the distribution ingress. ONE mapping serves every
distributor: the path carries a chi route parameter, cerberus stamps it as the
x-param-distribution_id header, and the per-distributor isolation comes from the
msr- key, whose AllowEndpoints names one CONCRETE path. Measured: the pilot key
scoped to /d/DIST-PILOT-1/rate is 401'd on /d/DIST-OTHER-9/rate and on /decision.
So the per-distributor provisioning cost is one KEY each, not one mapping each --
cheaper than plan section 8.7 assumed, and the key is the thing that must be
checked for, since the mapping is shared and always present.

mapping_version.description: Distribution ingress: broker submit for one distributor

_comment: One per distributor. gateway_id is the ACCOUNT's gateway id and path is the
concrete mapping path -- cerberus matches `/{gateway_id}{path}` against the
request, and on a tenant gateway the request path it sees is prefixed with the
gateway id. Measured: gateway_id "" or a first-path-segment value is refused;
gateway_id VWqPwSvI9DMS with path /decision is accepted on POST /decision and
Restricted keys default to 90 days and GET /accounts/api-keys is supposed to
stop returning key material -- record the key at mint time regardless.

traps: A digit-only value in config.static reaches the engine as a NUMBER: the flows MCP's jsonValue preprocess JSON.parses any digit-leading string. publisher_account_id "9227248058" arrived as 9227248058 and the submission write 400'd on schema validation. Coerce with String() inside the eval.

A `flow` node's payload object IS the sub-flow's $.trigger, flat. get_node_type_reference("flow") documents a nested payload.payload; sending that makes the sub-flow read $.trigger.payload.* -- and flow 1 then normalises every fact to __unanswered and would have rated a BLANK submission rather than failing, had the occupation lookup not errored first.
x-url on a tenant gateway is /<gateway-id>/<mapping path>, NOT the path the client sent. Parse a route segment from the END, or use x-param-<name>.

An http node discards the response body on 4xx, so a rejected record write surfaces only as "the function errored with status 400". The failing node id is in list_errored_workflows; reproduce the write directly to see the reason.

Every records filter here is an exact keyword match in STORED case. Lowercasing a keyword filter returns zero hits with no error -- the lowercase rule applies to analysed text fields (prefix search), never to keyword equality. `folder` is queryable the same way even though it is not an index_fields entry.
